source_text: ΙΘʹ. Δεινὸν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἁλῶναι, καὶ γλώσσῃ τρωθῆναι, καὶ ἀκοῇ δελεασθῆναι, καὶ διὰ θυμοῦ ζέσαντος ἐμπρησθῆναι, καὶ γεύσει κατενεχθῆναι, καὶ ἁφῇ μαλακισθῆναι, καὶ τοῖς ὅπλοις τῆς σωτηρίας, ὅπλοις θανάτου χρήσασθαι· δέον τῷ θυρεῷ φραξαμένους τῆς πίστεως, στῆναι πρὸς τὰς μεθοδείας τοῦ Πονηροῦ· καὶ μετὰ Χριστοῦ νικήσαντας, καὶ μετὰ τῶν μαρτύρων ἀθλήσαντας, τῆς μεγάλης ἐκείνης ἀκοῦσαι φωνῆς· Δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ Πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἐπηγγελμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν, ἔνθα εὐφραινομένων πάντων ἡ κατοικία, καὶ χορευόντων χορείαν τὴν ἀκατάλυτον· ἔνθα ἦχος ἑορταζόν των, καὶ φωνὴ ἀγαλλιάσεως, καὶ θεότητος ἔλλαμψις τελεωτέρα καὶ καθωτέρα, ἧς νῦν ἐν αἰνίγμασι καὶ σκιαῖς ἡ ἀπόλαυσις. Τούτοις Κυπριανὸς χαίρει μᾶλλον τιμώμενος, ἢ πᾶσιν ὁμοῦ τοῖς ἄλλοις· ταῦτα καὶ παρὼν ἐφιλοσόφει τῷ βίῳ, καὶ ἀπὼν πᾶσι διακελεύεται διὰ τῆς ἡμετέρας φωνῆς· ἣν μηδαμῶς ἀτιμάσητε, εἴπερ τι μέλει τῆς ἐκείνου καρτερίας ὑμῖν, καὶ τῶν ἐκείνου περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας ἀγωνισμάτων, κἀμοῦ τοῦ ταῦτα πρεσβεύοντος. Αὗταί σοι τῶν ἐμῶν λόγων αἱ ἀπαρχαὶ, ὦ θεία καὶ ἱερὰ κεφαλή· τοῦτό σοι καὶ τῶν λόγων γέρας καὶ τῆς ἀθλήσεως· οὐ κότινος Ὀλυμπιακὸς, οὔτε μῆλα Δελφικὰ παίγνια, οὐδὲ Ἰσθμικὴ πίτυς, οὐδὲ Νεμαίας σέλινα, δι' ὧν ἔφηβοι δυστυχεῖς ἐτιμήθησαν· ἀλλὰ λόγος, τὸ πάντων οἰκειότατον τοῖς Λόγου θεραπευταῖς· εἰ δὲ καὶ τῶν σῶν ἄθλων καὶ λόγων ἄξιον, τοῦ Λόγου τὸ δῶρον. Σὺ δὲ ἡμᾶς ἐποπτεύοις ἄνωθεν ἵλεως, καὶ τὸν ἡμέτερον διεξάγοις λόγον καὶ βίον, καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν τοῦτο ποίμνιον ποιμαίνοις, ἢ συμποιμαίνοις, τά τε ἄλλα εὐθύνων ὡς οἷόν τε πρὸς τὸ βέλτιστον, καὶ τοὺς βαρεῖς λύκους ἀποπεμπόμενος, τοὺς θηρευτὰς τῶν συλλαβῶν καὶ τῶν λέξεων· καὶ τὴν τῆς ἁγίας Τριάδος ἔλλαμψιν, ἧς σὺ νῦν παραστάτης, τελεωτέραν τε καὶ λαμπροτέραν ἡμῖν χαριζόμενος, ἣν προσκυνοῦμεν, ἣν δοξάζομεν, ᾗ συμπολιτευόμεθα, προσκυνοῦντες Πατέρα ἐν Υἱῷ, Υἱὸν ἐν ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, ᾗ καὶ παρασταίημεν ὕστερον εἰλικρινεῖς καὶ ἀπρόσκοποι, ἧς καὶ μεταλάβοιμεν τέλειοι τελείως, ἐν αὐτῷ Χριστῷ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, ᾧ πᾶσα δόξα, τιμὴ καὶ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The eternal reward and final doxology
orientation: Gregory is closing the oration, contrasting the dangers of the senses with the eternal joy promised to those who conquer with Christ, and he offers his speech as a gift to Cyprian before a final prayer and doxology.
pass_a_gloss: It is terrible to be captured by the eyes, and to be wounded by the tongue, and to be lured by hearing, and to be set on fire through boiling anger, and to be brought down by taste, and to be weakened by touch, and to use the weapons of salvation as weapons of death; when it is necessary, having fenced ourselves with the shield of faith, to stand against the schemes of the Evil One; and having conquered with Christ, and having contended with the martyrs, to hear that great voice: Come, you who are blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom promised to you, where is the dwelling of all who rejoice, and of those who dance a dance that cannot be dissolved; where is the sound of those who keep festival, and the voice of exultation, and a more perfect and purer illumination of divinity, of which now the enjoyment is in riddles and shadows. In these things Cyprian rejoices, being honored more than in all other things together; these things both when present he practiced as philosophy in his life, and when absent he commands to all through our voice; which do not dishonor in any way, if indeed you have any care for his endurance, and for his contests on behalf of the truth, and for me who advocates these things. These are for you the firstfruits of my words, O divine and sacred head; this is for you both the reward of the words and of the contest; not Olympic wild olive, nor Delphic apples as playthings, nor Isthmian pine, nor Nemean celery, by which unfortunate youths were honored; but a word, the most fitting of all things for the servants of the Word; and if it is worthy of your contests and words, the gift of the Word. But may you watch over us from above, gracious, and may you guide our word and life, and may you shepherd this sacred flock, or shepherd it together with us, directing other things as far as possible toward the best, and sending away the heavy wolves, the hunters of syllables and of words; and granting to us the illumination of the holy Trinity, of which you are now an attendant, more perfect and more brilliant, which we worship, which we glorify, with which we live as citizens, worshiping the Father in the Son, the Son in the Holy Spirit, with which may we also stand before it later, sincere and without offense, of which may we also partake, perfect ones perfectly, in Christ himself our Lord, to whom be all glory, honor, and might unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.term: ὅπλοις τῆς σωτηρίας, ὅπλοις θανάτου χρήσασθαι
choices.english: to use the weapons of salvation as weapons of death
choices.why: Keeps the parallel structure of the Greek, where the same noun 'weapons' is repeated with contrasting genitives, preserving the paradox.
rejected: to turn the weapons of salvation into weapons of death

choices.why: Matches the brief's marking of the quotation as introduced by 'that great voice' (τῆς μεγάλης ἐκείνης φωνῆς), preserving the demonstrative force.

choices.english: a dance that cannot be dissolved
choices.why: Renders ἀκατάλυτον literally as 'that cannot be dissolved' rather than 'unending,' preserving the image of a dance that no one can break up.
Keeps the literal pairing of 'riddles' and 'shadows,' echoing 1 Corinthians 13:12 language without smoothing it into 'dimly' or 'obscurely.'

choices.term: οἱ θηρευταὶ τῶν συλλαβῶν καὶ τῶν λέξεων
choices.english: the hunters of syllables and of words
choices.why: Preserves the metaphor of hunting and the precise objects 'syllables' and 'words,' which Gregory uses to mock pedantic critics.
rejected: the quibblers over syllables and words

choices.why: Renders the compound verb literally as 'live as citizens with,' reflecting the glossary's 'way of life' sense for πολιτεία and the communal, civic metaphor.

pass_b_english: It is a terrible thing to be captured through the eyes, wounded through speech, lured through the ear, set ablaze through seething anger, dragged down through taste, softened through touch, and to use the weapons of salvation as weapons of death. We ought rather to fence ourselves with the shield of faith and stand against the schemes of the Evil One, and after conquering with Christ and contending with the martyrs, to hear that great voice: “Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom promised to you” (Matthew 25:34), where all who rejoice have their dwelling, and they dance a dance that cannot be dissolved; where there is the sound of those keeping festival and the voice of gladness, and a more perfect and purer illumination of the Godhead, whose enjoyment now comes in riddles and shadows.

Cyprian rejoices to be honored by these things more than by all others put together. These are what he pursued as his philosophy in his life while he was present, and what he now urges upon you all through my voice, though he is absent. Do not dishonor that voice in any way, if you care at all for his steadfast endurance and his contests on behalf of the truth, and for me who commends these things to you.

These are the firstfruits of my words to you, O divine and holy head. This is my gift of honor to you, both for your words and for your contest: not an Olympic wild olive, not Delphic apples, those playthings, not Isthmian pine, not the celery of Nemea, with which unfortunate youths were honored, but a word, the thing most fitting of all for those who serve the Word. And if it is worthy of your contests and your words, it is the gift of the Word.

May you watch over us from above with favor, and guide our word and our life, and shepherd this holy flock, or shepherd it together with us, directing all things as far as possible toward what is best, and driving away the heavy wolves, the hunters of syllables and of expressions. And may you grant us a more perfect and brighter illumination of the Holy Trinity, of which you are now an attendant, whom we worship, whom we glorify, in whose city we live as fellow-citizens, worshiping the Father in the Son, the Son in the Holy Spirit. May we also stand beside it in the end, sincere and without offense, and may we perfectly share in it, perfected ones, in Christ himself our Lord, to whom be all glory, honor, and might forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: the hunters of syllables and of words
problems.source_quote: τοὺς θηρευτὰς τῶν συλλαβῶν καὶ τῶν λέξεων
problems.why: These are not 'heavy wolves' but a separate category: hunters who attack syllables and expressions, i.e., verbal critics.
problems.fix: and driving away the heavy wolves, and the hunters of syllables and of expressions
problems.ruling: τοὺς θηρευτὰς is appositive to λύκους, not separate: 'wolves, the hunters of syllables'

problems.why: παραστάτης is 'parastates,' one who stands beside/attends, not 'before whom you stand'; Cyprian serves as attendant/parastates of the Trinity.
problems.fix: of which you are now parastates/attendant
problems.ruling: ἧς σὺ νῦν παραστάτης: Cyprian is the Trinity's attendant, not one before whom Cyprian stands. Subject/object reversed.

problems.quote: May we stand before that Trinity in the end
problems.why: παρασταίημεν echoes παραστάτης above; 'stand beside/attend' not 'stand before'; and ᾗ is dative, 'before whom' misrepresents the relationship.
problems.fix: May we also stand beside it in the end
problems.ruling: παρασταίημεν echoes παραστάτης; 'stand beside/attend' not 'stand before.' ᾗ is dative of the Trinity, relationship misrendered.

edits.old: and driving away the heavy wolves, the hunters of syllables and of words.
edits.new: and driving away the heavy wolves, and the hunters of syllables and of expressions.
of which you are now an attendant

edits.old: May we stand before that Trinity in the end
edits.new: May we also stand beside it in the end

fixed: Corrected 'the hunters of syllables and of words' to 'and the hunters of syllables and of expressions' to reflect that the hunters are a separate category from the wolves, not appositional.
Corrected 'before whom you now stand' to 'of which you are now an attendant' to render παραστάτης as attendant rather than standing before.
Corrected 'May we stand before that Trinity in the end' to 'May we also stand beside it in the end' to echo παραστάτης and render the dative ᾗ as 'beside it' rather than 'before whom'.

problems.why: γλῶσσα here means language/speech (temptation through what is said), not the physical tongue as organ.

fixed: Changed 'wounded through the tongue' to 'wounded through speech' because γλῶσσα here means language/speech, not the physical organ.

problems.quote: with whom we live as citizens
problems.why: συμπολιτευόμεθα means 'live as fellow-citizens with', dative ᾗ refers to Trinity, but 'with whom' blurs that we live WITH the Trinity
problems.fix: in whose city we live as fellow-citizens

problems.quote: share in it perfectly, as those made perfect
problems.why: τελείως modifies μεταλάβοιμεν 'perfectly share', not 'as those made perfect'
problems.fix: perfectly share in it, perfected ones
problems.ruling: τέλειοι is nominative plural adjective ('we who are perfect'), not adverb; 'as those made perfect' mistranslates.

edits.old: with whom we live as citizens
edits.new: in whose city we live as fellow-citizens

edits.old: share in it perfectly, as those made perfect
edits.new: perfectly share in it, perfected ones

fixed: Changed 'with whom we live as citizens' to 'in whose city we live as fellow-citizens' to reflect συμπολιτευόμεθα as living as fellow-citizens with the Trinity.
Changed 'share in it perfectly, as those made perfect' to 'perfectly share in it, perfected ones' to reflect τελείως modifying μεταλάβοιμεν and τέλειοι as a nominative plural.

problems.quote: while he was present in the body
problems.why: τῷ βίῳ is the life by which he philosophized; “in the body” is not in the Greek and misplaces that phrase.
problems.fix: These he lived as his philosophy while he was present, and while absent he urges them on everyone through my voice.
problems.ruling: ἐφιλοσόφει τῷ βίῳ means he practiced philosophy by his life (dative of means); 'in the body' is invented and changes the sense.

edits.old: These are what he pursued as his philosophy while he was present in the body, and what he now urges upon you all through my voice, though he is absent
edits.new: These are what he pursued as his philosophy in his life while he was present, and what he now urges upon you all through my voice, though he is absent

edits.old: and driving away the heavy wolves, and the hunters of syllables and of expressions
edits.new: and driving away the heavy wolves, the hunters of syllables and of expressions

fixed: mistranslation `in the body`: fixed — παρὼν ἐφιλοσόφει τῷ βίῳ means he philosophized in/by his life while present; no body word in Greek.
wolves/hunters `and`: fixed — source τοὺς βαρεῖς λύκους, τοὺς θηρευτὰς has no καί, second phrase is apposition, so removed added `and`.
attendant: no edit — ἧς σὺ νῦν παραστάτης supports `of which you are now an attendant`.
stand beside it: no edit — ᾗ καὶ παρασταίημεν supports `stand beside it`, καί = also.
wounded through speech: no edit — γλώσσῃ can mean speech, no misstatement of sense.
in whose city / fellow-citizens: no edit — συμπολιτευόμεθα contains fellow-citizenship idea, literary rendering stands.
perfectly share / perfected ones: no edit — ἧς μεταλάβοιμεν τέλειοι τελείως supports adverb + nominative rendering.

refereed.quote: in whose city we live as fellow-citizens
refereed.why: συμπολιτευόμεθα means 'live together as citizens', not 'in whose city'
refereed.ruling: συμπολιτευόμεθα means 'we live as fellow-citizens together'; 'in whose city' adds a noun not in source.
